title: Security hacknotebook — control sketches & prep thread
body:
Quick brain-dump while iterating the SOC2 evidence map. Mostly fragments, will later move cleaned items to the controls spreadsheet and Confluence page.

Goal: get a small, reviewable subset of control families with minimal evidence friction for first external readiness review (Q2 target). Keep it pragmatic — engineering-friendly evidence where possible.

Top-level plan (sketch):
- pick 6-8 controls to validate end-to-end by end of sprint
- map each control -> evidence artifacts we already have (logs, dashboards, runbooks, PRs, contracts)
- identify holes and lowest-effort remediation steps
- consolidate answers into customer-facing control narrative (one-pager each)

Notes / shorthand (won't be pretty):
- Access control (A1): currently: Okta SSO + SCIM -> GSuite + internal RBAC in Console backend. Evidence candidates: Okta export (audit logs), SCIM provisioning job PR, Console role matrix CSV (generated patch).
  - Quick ask: Lena to pull Okta export for Feb 2026 (help: jira SEC-712).
  - Open question: service accounts created by infra pipelines — where do we record them? existing inventory (infra-kv) is incomplete. TODO: script to dump service-account list from k8s namespaces.

- Change mgmt (A2): PR review + CI gating. Evidence: GitHub branch protection settings screenshot, required-reviewers list, deployment runbook (doc id: confluence:deploy-runbook-9).
  - Gap: emergency change log — we have Slack announcements but no single archived emergency-change register. Proposed light fix: a dedicated GH issue template for emergency-change that auto-labels and links to CI artifacts. Low effort.

- Logging & monitoring (A3): centralized logging to ELK + Cloud metrics. Evidence: example log retention policy snippet, alert channel configuration (PagerDuty integration), dashboard snapshots for high-severity alerts.
  - Notes: retention policy technically in SRE Confluence page, but need a direct exported JSON config or screenshot with timestamp.

- Incident response (A4): playbooks exist, tabletop cadence monthly. Evidence: last 3 tabletop notes, incident timelines (postmortem PRs), PagerDuty rotation schedule.
  - Hole: postmortem template incomplete around RCA sign-off. Quick patch: add RCA owner field and signature line to template (one-line change).

- Vendor mgmt / data handling (A5): third-party vendors have contracts + DPA for major vendors. Evidence: signed DPAs in legal drive (link later), vendor inventory sheet (sheet id: vendors-2025).
  - Gap: small SaaS tools used by teams not inventoried. Quick step: send a short stake-holder survey (one email) to engineering leads asking for tools with access to PII or logs.

- Cryptography / key mgmt (A6): KMS in cloud for production keys, HSM for payment tokens. Evidence: KMS policy doc, KMS key rotation logs, KMS IAM bindings screenshot.
  - Q: are any legacy keys stored in repo? quick grep (repo: infra-config) scheduled. Omar volunteered to run.

Evidence mapping (rough matrix, one-line per control):
- A1 Access control -> Okta export (audit.csv), Console role-matrix.csv, PR#1342 (scim fixes), incident ticket if provisioning error exists
- A2 Change mgmt -> branch-protection.json screenshot, PR merge graph for last 90 days, deploy-runbook-9, emergency-change GH issues (proposed)
- A3 Logging/monitoring -> log-retention-policy.md, dashboard-alert-ops.png, pagerduty-integrations.csv, metric-export-2026-02-01.json
- A4 Incident response -> postmortem-2026-01-12.md, tabletop-notes-feb-2026.docx, pagerduty-rotation.png
- A5 Vendor mgmt -> vendor-inventory-2025.csv, signed-dpa-letter-2024.pdf, procurement-ticket-4567
- A6 Key mgmt -> kms-policy-v1.md, key-rotation-logs-2026-02.log, hsm-contract.pdf

Immediate low-effort wins (for next 2 weeks):
- produce screenshots/exports for Okta (A1) and GH branch protection (A2) — quick 15m ops tasks.
- create emergency-change GH issue template (A2) — PR + merge in 1 day.
- export dashboard snapshots and retention policy excerpt (A3) — ask monitoring team.
- add RCA owner field to postmortem template (A4) — 10m doc edit.

Open/risks/questions (unresolved):
- How aggressive do we need to be on creating new artifacts? External auditors prefer "native" artifacts over created-for-audit screenshots but pragmatic approach OK for first pass. Need PM/Legal alignment.
- Inventory completeness: do we accept team-level attestation for small tools? If yes, what attestation wording is sufficient?
- Data classification: ID sensitive buckets/indices and owners (SRE + infra to help).
- Retention numbers accuracy: logs/metrics retention vary by system, need consolidated table. Who maintains canonical retention mapping? (ops? infra?).

Notes to self / process reminders:
- keep evidence timestamps; auditor loves time-bounded exports (e.g., Okta export with date).
- prefer exported CSV/JSON over screenshots when possible.
- tag each evidence artifact with control id and short narrative (1-2 lines) before uploading to Confluence evidence repo.

Draft email text for engineering leads (short):
"Quick ask: please reply with any SaaS/tool used by your team that stores customer data, logs, or PII. One-line per tool. We need this for the vendor inventory update for SOC readiness. Deadline: 2026-03-12."

Quick todo list (bullet):
- [ ] Lena: Okta exports (Feb) + example user provisioning event (due 2026-03-08)
- [ ] Omar: repo grep for hard-coded keys (infra-config), run and share results (due 2026-03-07)
- [ ] Me (Dante): emergency-change template PR + create GH issue label (due 2026-03-05)
- [ ] Marta: compile vendor inventory CSV + attach DPAs (ongoing, checkpoint 2026-03-10)

Slightly longer thoughts (raw):
- We should aim for narratives that map technical artefacts to business risk. e.g., rather than just "Okta export", note that "Okta provisioning logs show SCIM created N users with role X; this demonstrates automated deprovisioning for employees". Auditors want the 'so what'.
- For infra-service accounts, maybe treat them as a separate control note: account lifecycle (creation, rotation, decommission) — short checklist and an automated report (weekly) would satisfy the sample requirement.

Where to file cleaned artifacts: Confluence evidence repo (page id above) + attach to audit tracker ticket jira:SEC-712. Keep filenames consistent: controlid_evidence_YYYYMMDD.<ext>

Last reminders: keep this doc messy. Move only finished narratives to Confluence. If someone else finds this, feel free to comment inline.

-- end of hacknotebook entry (Dante)
